messages.subject: Dynamic model
parts:
Dear all,

I wonder if INLA can be used for the following dynamic model. Suppose that i have matrices and vectors: x[t,1:2], a[t,1:2,1:2], y[t,1:2], w[t,1:2]
The model is:
x[t,] = x[t-1,] + u[t]
a[t,1,] = logit(x[t,])
a[t,2,] = 1 - a[t,1,]
y[t] = a[t,,]%*%w[t,] + v[t]
w are known weights. u,v are iid multivariate gaussian noise.

Thanks in advance,
Tiep.

parts:
I just realize a typo in the previous post. It should be logistic, not logit function.

Thanks,
Tiep.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Dynamic model
parts:
Assume the third dimension of a[] is 2, then the mean of y[t] depends
on

.. * ilink(x[t,1]) + .. * ilink(x[t,2]) + ..

where '..' is 'some constant'. sorry, INLA cannot do this, because the
right hand side of (or the mean of y[t])

is then a non-linear function of several x[,]'s, which violate the
assumption made that each data-point only depends on one node in the
latent field.

if the third dimension of a[] is 1, then its ok.... but I guess that is
not that interesting case.
